title: Deprecated and Insecure Module Usage Static Analysis Rules

rules.name: Import of a deprecated or insecure standard library module
rules.description: The module telnetlib, ftplib, imp, cgi or pickletools is imported. These are removed from the standard library in Python 3.11-3.13 or are documented as unsafe: telnetlib and ftplib send credentials in clear text, imp is superseded by importlib and blocks the import system, and cgi has a long history of parsing and injection flaws. pickletools is not a safe loader for untrusted data.
rules.remediation_example: import subprocess  # replace telnetlib with paramiko over SSH, ftplib with sftp, imp with importlib, cgi with a maintained web framework

rules.name: Weak TLS protocol version selected
rules.description: A TLS context is built with ssl.PROTOCOL_TLSv1, ssl.PROTOCOL_TLSv1_1, ssl.PROTOCOL_SSLv3 or the deprecated ssl.PROTOCOL_SSLv23 alias. TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are withdrawn by RFC 8996 and permit downgrade and padding-oracle attacks; SSLv3 is broken by POODLE.
rules.remediation_example: context = ssl.create_default_context()  # negotiates TLS 1.2+; never pin PROTOCOL_TLSv1 or PROTOCOL_SSLv23
